ann.l: Call-Exner bodies: These tiny, follicle-like spaces are ringed by tumor cells and contain eosinophilic (pink) secretions. They mimic normal developing follicles and are the classic diagnostic hallmark of granulosa cell tumors.

Diffuse sheets of uniform cells: The tumor is composed of a monotonous population of small, round-to-oval cells with scant cytoplasm. The nuclei resemble normal granulosa cells and show minimal atypia.
Fibrovascular stroma: This prominent band of pink collagenous tissue containing blood vessels runs diagonally, dividing the sheets of granulosa cells into lobules or nests.

findings: Call-Exner bodies: tiny round, follicle-like spaces ringed by tumor cells and often holding pink material are scattered through the sheets; they are the classic hallmark of a granulosa cell tumor.
Diffuse sheets of small, uniform cells: monotonous round to oval nuclei with scant cytoplasm show a single population that resembles follicular granulosa cells.
Fibrovascular stroma: a band of pink fibrous tissue with thin vessels runs diagonally through the lower left, separating the solid sheets of tumor into regions.
